title: Lesson 4 - Implementation Considerations Across Sales and Marketing
description: Given a scenario, discuss common sales and marketing processes and anticipate key implementation considerations.

questions.question: You enable Enterprise Territory Management and want opportunity access to follow territories. What must be true for that access to work?
options: The role hierarchy must be deleted first
Territory assignment rules only ever assign accounts, never opportunities
The territory model must be active and have opportunity assignment rules
Every user must hold the Sales Engagement license
questions.explanation: Territory-based opportunity access only takes effect once the model is activated and opportunity assignment rules are in place, while the role hierarchy is not deleted and licenses are unrelated.

questions.question: A sales manager wants forecast rollups by product family in addition to total revenue. What do you configure?
options: Multiple forecast types in Collaborative Forecasts
A new territory type in the territory model
Customizable Campaign Influence for the pipeline
Einstein Activity Capture for the forecast managers
questions.explanation: Forecast types let Collaborative Forecasts roll up by revenue, quantity, or product family side by side, whereas territory, influence, and activity capture do not produce forecast rollups.

questions.question: An org turns on Einstein Activity Capture and later finds that reports built on standard Task records look empty. Why?
options: The Einstein Trust Layer blocks Task creation for those users
Activity Capture stores email and events in an external store, so they are not standard Task rows
Sales Engagement deletes Tasks when a cadence completes
Territory assignment rules remove the Task records from reports
questions.explanation: Captured email and events live in an external store related to records rather than as Task rows, which is why Task-based reports undercount the captured activity.
